subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class cron-scoped tool policy, make cron inherit subagent policy, or keep per-job `payload.toolsAllow` as the only hard cron tool boundary?
rationale: The choice defines a public config surface and enforcement boundary for scheduled automation, including whether existing announce jobs keep direct `message` access by default.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent typed cron policy with explicit precedence, docs, config metadata, and tests for announce/message behavior.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat isolated cron sessions as a policy peer of subagents so `tools.subagents.tools` also applies to cron, accepting and documenting the broader coupling.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Decline a global cron config surface and document that operators must use per-job `payload.toolsAllow` or runtime delivery safeguards for cron restrictions.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` or an equivalent typed cron policy with explicit precedence, docs, config metadata, and tests for announce/message behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across scoped conversation capability profiles, cron/session behavior, and prior review context for this issue.
